chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) — or said: the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) — said: 'Women are of four types: one who gathers and unites, one who is like a flourishing spring bringing fertility, one who is a crushing distress, and one who is a filthy yoke.'

key_terms.جَامِعٌ مُجْمِعٌ: one who gathers and unifies — the ideal wife who brings harmony to the household
key_terms.رَبِيعٌ مُرْبِعٌ: a spring-like woman — fertile, nurturing, and bringing prosperity
key_terms.غُلٌّ قَمِلٌ: a filthy neck-shackle — a degrading and shameful burden
key_terms.كَرْبٌ مُقْمِعٌ: a crushing distress — a burden that overwhelms and suppresses

ai.seo_question: What are the four types of women described in a hadith of Imam al-Sadiq from the Prophet or Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith, reported through the isnad of al-Sakuni from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), preserves a saying attributed to either the Prophet (SAWW) or Imam Ali (AS) — the narrator's uncertainty itself being recorded faithfully — that classifies women into four character types using rhyming Arabic imagery: the blessed unifier, the fertile spring-like woman, the burden of distress, and the shameful yoke. The saying reflects a pre-Islamic Arabic rhetorical tradition of character typology expressed in vivid, compressed verse-like forms, adapted here within an Islamic ethical framework to emphasize the import of choosing a righteous spouse.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

(it was said) either by ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> or ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Four features are amalgamated in women, the goodness, and a desire for children, and a tint of anguish, and the dominance’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, or ‘Amir al- Mu’minin has said, ‘Women are of four kinds: a universal goodness, a fountain of breeding, an oppressive over-burdening or feed for parasites.”’
